summary: Wuhan suits broad, energetic city travel built around river views, lake spaces, historic campuses, and a strong everyday food culture.
transport_notes: Wuhan is spread across several major zones, so each day should stay clustered around one riverbank, one lake area, or one historic district.
Metro is useful, but avoid combining East Lake, Hankou old streets, and riverfront landmarks in a single tight day.
Evening plans work best near riverside promenades, food-heavy neighborhoods, or walkable civic-center pockets.

budget_notes.low: Prioritize public lakefront areas, river walks, and practical neighborhood food streets.
budget_notes.medium: Combine one landmark or campus area, one scenic public space, and one recognizable local dining zone each day.
budget_notes.high: Use fewer cross-city jumps, stronger dining stops, and more comfort-oriented pacing between larger sites.

trip_type_notes.student: Student plans in Wuhan should feel lively, affordable, and rooted in local food plus youth-heavy city spaces.
trip_type_notes.solo: Solo plans should emphasize observation, riverside wandering, and broad city texture without overpacking routes.
trip_type_notes.couple: Couple plans should soften Wuhan's scale with river lights, lake views, and quieter evening pacing.
trip_type_notes.family: Family plans should keep movement simple and use broad public spaces and landmark clarity to reduce fatigue.
